artifact_purpose: GitHub AI implementation guide for rebuilding cbenton.art Samples as a project index with project-level detail pages.

site.primary_change: Samples must become a project index. Individual image filenames and player names must not define projects.

scrape_and_audit_status.result: The current site did not return reliable searchable/indexed pages to the available crawler during this pass, and direct runtime DNS access was unavailable. Treat repository inspection as authoritative for current implementation details.
implementation_instruction: Before editing, inspect the repository routes, current Samples component/page, sample asset directory, any existing project metadata, and all links that currently point into Samples.
Do not infer the site's current route tree from filenames.
Do not delete or rename assets merely to make routing easier.
Use this JSON as the desired information architecture and explicit asset-to-project manifest.

critical_correction.statement: Solomon Williams, EJ Caminong, Jaron Keawe Sagapolutele, Emmanuel Okoye, Ian Strong, AJ Tuitele, Jackson Brousseau, Aaron Hampton, Angus Davies, Frederick Williams III, Justin Hasenhuetl, and Rico Walker are NOT separate projects.
critical_correction.rule: Player-specific images are instances/examples inside the UC Berkeley — I’M COOL project page.
forbidden_behavior: Do not generate one project card per player.
Do not generate one project route per player.
Do not derive project titles from player filenames.
Do not treat jersey number or origin as a project category.
Do not show player names as peer-level navigation beside actual project titles.

samples_index.headline: Selected project systems
samples_index.intro: Each project is shown as a system or body of related work. Individual images, editions, players, and variants live inside the project that generated them.

projects.title: UC Berkeley — I’M COOL
projects.short_description: A coded front/back visual system built as one UC Berkeley project, with player-specific data producing related but distinct units inside a consistent graphic architecture.
positioning_notes: Present this as one system with many outputs.
Use the overview front/back images to explain the base visual architecture.
Use the player-specific images to demonstrate controlled variation.
The value of the page is the relationship between the units, not the celebrity or identity of any one player.

index_card.title: UC Berkeley — I’M COOL
index_card.summary: One visual grammar, expanded across player-specific front/back units.

detail_page.intro_copy: The player names, jersey numbers, origins, and other variable information are inputs to the system. They are not separate project identities. The project page should first establish the shared front/back architecture, then show how that architecture changes from unit to unit.

sections.heading: Player-specific instances
sections.description: Show all player units as examples generated by the same parent system. Captions may include player, jersey number, and origin, but captions must remain visually subordinate to the project title.

recommended_card_content: small scope marker such as '12 instances' or '8 variants'
card_behavior: Entire card links to the parent project route.
Do not link directly to raw image files from the index.
Do not place player names in index-card headlines.
Do not use filename numbers as visible ranking or chronology.

responsive_behavior.desktop: 2-column or editorial asymmetric grid depending on existing design system
responsive_behavior.mobile: single-column project cards with uncropped or lightly constrained project imagery

project_page_component_model.implementation_note: Render from structured project data. Do not scan the samples directory and auto-create project pages from every image.

routing_rules.legacy_behavior: If the current repository already has asset-level or player-level routes, redirect them to the appropriate parent project rather than keeping them as independent portfolio entries.

filename_handling.principle: Filenames are source metadata, not public information architecture.
rules: Never convert every file basename into a project title.
Never infer parent project from the first numeric prefix alone.
The repeated 01_, 02_, etc. prefixes exist in multiple families and must not be globally sorted as one project sequence.
Use the explicit project manifest in this JSON.
Preserve original files on disk unless there is a strong repository reason to rename them.

avoid: client claims not supported by repository content
content_and_copy_rules.accuracy_rule: Do not imply UC Berkeley commissioned, approved, licensed, or endorsed the I’M COOL work unless repository content explicitly proves that relationship.

github_ai_execution_order: 1. Audit existing /samples route and sample-related components.
2. Inventory all sample assets and confirm the listed paths exist.
3. Create structured project data using this manifest.
5. Create a reusable /samples/{slug} project detail template.
6. Implement UC Berkeley — I’M COOL first and verify that all 12 player images appear inside that one project.
7. Implement BOOTYZ as one project with eight variants.
9. Resolve the canonical name for the Christopher phone-stack asset from repository context; use the working title only if no better title exists.
10. Repair internal links and add redirects only where existing routes require them.
11. Test responsive image behavior, alt text, keyboard navigation, metadata, and production build.
acceptance_tests: The /samples page shows project cards rather than one card for every PNG.
Solomon Williams is not a project title on /samples.
All player-specific UC Berkeley images live on /samples/uc-berkeley-im-cool.
The UC Berkeley project page visibly explains that the player images are instances of one visual system.
BOOTYZ appears once on the Samples index and contains eight variants on its detail page.
IT’S HER BIRTHDAY appears once as a project.
The Christopher phone-stack image appears once under a parent project rather than as eight inferred projects.
Raw filename prefixes are not visible as project hierarchy.
No unsupported claims of commissioning, endorsement, licensing, or client relationship are introduced.
The repository build, lint, and type checks pass after the restructure.
